title: Cost-Performance Formula — Definition & Consistent Application
description: Define a transparent, reproducible cost-performance scoring formula and apply it consistently to ALL comparison set items. The formula must: (1) Combine price, inference performance (tokens/s), and training feasibility into a single score, (2) Be weighted to reflect the user's primary use case (inference > training), (3) Account for VRAM capacity as a hard constraint (not just a soft score — if VRAM < model requirement, the item is disqualified for that workload), (4) Include a scenario modifier: the same GPU may score differently in S1 vs S3 because budget constraints change the weight of price vs performance, (5) Be fully documented: every weight, every normalization method, every assumption must be stated. Proposed formula structure (to be validated/refined): raw_score = w1 * (tokens_s / price) + w2 * (vram_capacity / max_vram) + w3 * (bandwidth / max_bandwidth) + w4 * training_score where w1+w2+w3+w4 = 1.0. The weights should reflect: inference throughput per dollar is most important (w1=0.5), VRAM capacity (w2=0.25), bandwidth (w3=0.15), training feasibility (w4=0.1). Apply this formula to all 9 hardware items + cloud baseline. Report the ranked list. Also compute scenario-specific scores: S1 weights (price=0.6, performance=0.25, VRAM=0.1, training=0.05), S3 weights (price=0.2, performance=0.4, VRAM=0.25, training=0.15). Document all normalization methods (min-max, log scale for price, etc.).
outputs: documented cost-performance formula with weights and normalization
ranked list of all comparison set items by cost-performance score
sensitivity analysis: how do scores change with weight variations?
VRAM hard-constraint analysis: which items fail for which model sizes?
